subject: Private Offer: soft-commit clawback mechanics and channel routing
messages:

Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — running numbers and channel split

Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at Horizon (we run multi-cloud buys for Cloudway) asked me to formalize two asks before we move to legal:

1) Soft-commit clawback — their finance team expects a 3-tier clawback schedule if we miss a 12-month spend target (25%/$ value for first 3 months of shortfall, then 15%, then 5%). They asked whether Redwood can accept a stepped-clawback tied to net invoice value after channel deductions.

2) Channel routing / reseller netback — we resell to end customers through Horizon and need a consistent reseller netback (they requested 18% net). If Redwood offers an 18% pass-through, can you preserve list-price anchoring for Marketplace reporting while reflecting the pass-through in payment flows?

I'm looping procurement to keep everything transparent. Attached is a basic proforma with our modeled consumption.

Thanks — can you share what flex you have on the clawback timings and whether a 18% netback is feasible without changing the list price reported to the marketplace?

—Kyle
Kyle Peterson
VP, Cloud Partnerships
Cloudway

Kyle — thanks for the clear breakdown and the proforma. Looping Ben for pricing and Irene for marketplace ops. Quick answers up front:

- Clawback: We can support a stepped clawback tied to net invoice value but prefer anchoring the trigger to committed SKUs/month rather than gross invoice to simplify reconciliation. That said, we can accept invoice-based clawbacks if Horizon signs off to the exception.

- Reseller netback: We can route payments such that Horizon receives an 18% netback; Redwood will still publish list-price for marketplace telemetry/reporting. That requires a private offer mapping in the marketplace (we'll show list price + discount lines) and a pass-through line in our settlement engine.

I'm attaching a short term-sheet sketch that shows the two flows (list-price reporting vs settlement pass-through). If you want, we can propose exact wording for the PO and a fallback if the clawback window needs compression.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben to confirm whether 18% netback is achievable under the requested discount depth and what that implies for Redwood net ARR.
- Irene to call out any marketplace compliance or reporting constraints.

I'll hold a 30-minute slot Wednesday to walk procurement through the term sheet if that helps.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Strategic GTM, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — margin impact and pro forma

Quick math from our side after plugging in the proforma:

- If we apply an 18% netback to Horizon as a straight pass-through, Redwood gross takes a ~11.5% hit on list revenue after marketplace fees (marketplace fee estimate 7%). That reduces our contribution margin materially unless we tier the effective discount by commit.

Options to keep Redwood economics acceptable: 
- Anchor list price at current levels, but apply an upfront volume rebate to Horizon (paid annually) rather than a monthly pass-through — improves cash flow predictability for Redwood.
- Keep monthly pass-through but tier it so netback is 18% only above a $1.2M trailing 12m spend; below that we step through 12/15/18%.
- Allow the clawback schedule Kyle proposed but compress the first period to 60 days (25% -> 15%) to reduce short-term exposure.

From a sales/commercial perspective I prefer the tiered pass-through — aligns incentives and preserves list-price telemetry. Happy to run detailed P&L if you want.

Ben Carter
Director, Marketplace Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Ben — thanks, the tiered pass-through approach is workable for Horizon if the thresholds are clear. Two follow-ups from procurement: 

1) Can Redwood confirm the settlement cadence (monthly vs quarterly) for the pass-through? They prefer quarterly reconciliations.
2) On the clawback compression — Horizon will accept 60 days for the first tier only if there is a written grace for first-time usage dips (one-time waiver).

Kyle Peterson
VP, Cloud Partnerships
Cloudway

Kyle / Horizon procurement —

We can do the following and I'll put it into a redlined term sketch for legal: 

- Settlement cadence: quarterly reconciliations for pass-through payments with month-level reporting (we'll issue detailed breakdowns each month and settle every quarter).
- Netback: tiered pass-through that reaches 18% only after $1.2M trailing 12-months; 12% below $400k, 15% between $400k and $1.2M. We'll show all lines in marketplace private-offer metadata so list-price telemetry is preserved.
- Clawback: accept the 3-tier clawback structure tied to net invoice value but compress first window to 60 days with a one-time first-year waiver for the first usage dip.
